X / Link payment data on a days-old account that surfaced old numbers and a previously reported email.
RBS Grade 4 / fraud logs and why I could not get a manager meeting or a clear account of unrecognised activity.
Chain of custody for cards and other items found at addresses, including who entered when, CCTV gaps, and why a gas engineer would already know about cards.
Whether statements attributed to named officials in tribunal/court papers were actually made by those people.

Today marks the day, almost a decade ago, when a group of 50 brokers attacked NoBroker. It was not the extent of the assault, but the surprise/shock of “Is it really happening?” What seemed like a local procession in front of our office-cum-residential house quickly revealed itself to be a group of people hell-bent on beating us and breaking computers/servers.

I ducked the next slap that was meant for me. When I tried to record it on my phone, it was quickly noticed by them. Our only saviour was the iron grill door through which we locked ourselves inside. Akhil and I had the look of “Ab kya karey?” on our faces. Next scene was us sitting in a police jeep going to the station, with brokers still continuing to create a ruckus at the office. We realised our complete lack of “connections,” with no IAS, IPS or politician on our speed-dial.

The day somehow ended, but the circumstances ensured that we had to vacate our office overnight and display “regret” messages on our website. Through the entire ordeal, somehow, it never crossed the minds of us three founders that NoBroker was at risk. Such is the power of optimism (or should I say misplaced innocence). Somehow, we struggled, the team grew stronger together, and we tried to survive one day at a time. 

Today, after Rs. 1,000 crore+ of yearly revenue and after serving 4 crore customers and saving thousands of crores in brokerage, we can afford to reminisce about it as an “incident” that happened. What did it teach us? Perseverance, optimism, the power of compounding and, above all, the power of “never giving up.”

#NoBroker #StartUp #India

The Grievance Appellate Committee (GAC), Ministry of Electronics & IT, by its Order dated 15 July 2026 (Appeal No. 8321/2026), has directed YouTube to remove the video within 24 hours of receiving the order.

Note: Although the order is dated 15.07.2026, it was uploaded publicly today (19 July 2026).

Key findings of the GAC:
• The video contains statements found to insult Bhagwan Shri Ram, Bhagwan Shri Krishna, and Sita Devi.
• It was found to make claims that they consumed meat and alcohol using disputed interpretations of scriptures.
• The GAC held that the content hurts the religious sentiments of crores of Hindus and is contrary to societal harmony.
• YouTube's free speech arguments were not accepted, with the order noting that freedom of expression is subject to the reasonable restrictions under Article 19(2) of the Constitution.

The order follows the Hon'ble Delhi High Court's direction dated 3 July 2026 requiring the appeal to be decided within 15 days.

The complainant has also stated that these findings may be relevant to a separate pending petition before a Magistrate seeking registration of an FIR against Dhruv Rathee, which is listed for hearing on 10 September 2026.

Statement : The blocking of BitChat's code on GitHub is unconstitutional and authoritarian. 

New Delhi, 24 July 2026

The Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) condemns the order issued by the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs, directing GitHub to remove the code repositories of BitChat. 

The order, Notice No. 11072601011432, was issued at 11:16 pm on 23 July 2026 under Section 79(3)(b) of the Information Technology Act, 2000 read with Rule 3(1)(d) of the IT Rules, 2021. The order directs GitHub to disable access to three repositories, including the Android application and its release files, within three hours. It threatens the platform with loss of safe harbour and criminal prosecution. No copy was published by the Government of India. The public learnt of it from a post by @jack, whose team develops BitChat. Censorship in India now comes to light through disclosure by the censored.

Since 17 July 2026, the Ministry of Home Affairs has suspended mobile internet around Jantar Mantar as per public reports about five times, most recently within a 1.5 kilometre radius from 4 pm until midnight on 23 July. That radius takes in Janpath and parts of Connaught Place. Reports describe signal jammers at the protest site and people walking two kilometres before their phones work. Inside that zone a student separated from her group during a detention drive cannot send a message to say where she is. Thousands of students and young people have camped at Jantar Mantar since June, seeking accountability for examination irregularities. Permission for their march to Parliament was refused. Metro stations were shut and also internet connectivity has been blocked.

BitChat is an open source application built for exactly this situation. It passes messages from phone to phone over Bluetooth, without mobile networks or a central server. It is striking that the order does not identify a single unlawful message. It objects to what BitChat is. In its own words, the application is dangerous because it enables communication "even during network restrictions" and can "circumvent lawful restrictions" during "internet shutdowns". Hence, the government's objection is that citizens can speak to one another while it has switched the internet off. 

The order is illegal on at least four grounds. 

1. Section 79(3)(b) is not a blocking power. In Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015) 5 SCC 1, the Supreme Court read down the provision. Intermediaries may be required to act only on a court order, or a government notification confined to the grounds under Article 19(2) of the Constitution. Blocking is governed exclusively by Section 69A and the Blocking Rules, 2009, which require a hearing and reasons recorded in writing, subject to review. Directions issued under Section 79(3)(b), Rule 3(1)(d) and the Sahyog Portal evade these safeguards, and constitutional challenges to this parallel regime are pending before High Courts. 

2. The reasons in the order are circular. The order asserts that the repositories contain "information which is prohibited under any law" without naming any such information, and rests on what the application is "capable of" enabling. Anticipated misuse of a communications tool is not a lawful basis to prohibit the tool. By this logic a telephone exchange could be sealed. 

3. The order cites Section 43 of the IT Act, a civil compensation provision, alongside conspiracy and abetment offences under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, against a platform that hosts code. 

4. A three hour deadline issued close to midnight forecloses legal assessment and recourse, and fails the proportionality standard in Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India (2020) 3 SCC 637.

The order also fails on its own terms as deleting a repository does not delete the application from any phone that carries it, and the mesh keeps functioning without servers. What the takedown actually prevents is scrutiny of the underlying code.

IFF demands that the Government of India:

1. Withdraw Notice No. 11072601011432 dated 23 July 2026 issued to GitHub.
2. Publish every takedown direction issued under Section 79(3)(b), Rule 3(1)(d) and the Sahyog Portal, with the reasons recorded for each.
3. Restore full connectivity around Jantar Mantar, publish all suspension orders, and disclose the legal authority for the deployment of jammers.

We stand with the developers and the young protesters whose speech this order seeks to silence.

Can the Government suspend a political party’s Instagram handle without a clear statutory power? And can a politician boycott a courtroom while simultaneously asking the Supreme Court to transfer the same judge from hearing his case?  

This week, the Aam Aadmi Party raised both questions in two different constitutional courtrooms.  

In the Supreme Court, AAP challenged the suspension of its Gujarat unit’s Instagram handle, arguing that Section 79(3)(b) of the IT Act was never meant to become a direct content-blocking weapon. 

Senior Advocate Shadan Farasat argued that the provision only deals with “safe harbour” obligations of intermediaries — not independent censorship powers.  The party says the move violates Article 19(1)(a), the constitutional guarantee of free speech. 

The Supreme Court has now issued notice to the Centre.  At the same time in the Delhi High Court, Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma appointed three amicus curiae for Arvind Kejriwal, Manish Sisodia, and Satyendar Jain after the leaders chose to boycott proceedings, invoking “Mahatma Gandhi’s Satyagraha principles” and claiming their faith in the court process had been shaken.  

But here’s the constitutional twist: Kejriwal had also moved the Supreme Court seeking transfer of the excise policy case away from Justice Sharma’s bench — even as his legal team withdrew from participation before her court.  

This has now created a rare constitutional confrontation involving: 
⚖️ Article 19 vs state regulation of digital speech 
⚖️ Article 21 vs procedural fairness in criminal prosecution 
⚖️ Judicial recusal vs courtroom boycott 
⚖️ Free speech, due process, and strategic constitutional litigation  Justice Sharma’s response may become one of the most significant procedural moments in the case: instead of proceeding ex parte, she chose to appoint independent senior advocates as amicus curiae to preserve procedural fairness.  

And one line from the Supreme Court hearing may define this entire battle: “Today my portal is gone.”  Because this is no longer just about an Instagram account.

 It is about whether opposition parties in India can lose their digital voice overnight — and what constitutional remedy exists when that happens.

INDIA CRACKS DOWN ON AI & DEEP FAKE. BIG TECH PUT ON NOTCE

1. What has actually changed?

The Modi government amended the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 on 10 February 2026 specifically to deal with synthetically generated information and deepfakes.
The framework covers deceptive AI-generated audio, visual and audio-visual material.
The idea is no longer simply: remove illegal content after somebody complains.

Platforms are now being pushed towards:
identification
labelling
metadata
verification
automated detection
rapid takedown
and greater accountability for allowing unlawful AI content to spread.

2. AI CONTENT HAS TO BE IDENTIFIABLE
This is probably the biggest structural change.
AI-generated/synthetically altered material covered by the rules has to be clearly identifiable as synthetic.
Platforms/services enabling generation or alteration of such content must ensure appropriate labels or traceable identifiers/metadata.
The objective is simple:
REAL CONTENT ≠ AI CONTENT
The viewer should not have to conduct a forensic investigation to figure out whether something was artificially generated.
Important nuance

Don't say “every piece of text written using AI anywhere on the internet must carry a label.”

MeitY's FAQ clarifies that the operative 2026 SGI definition primarily targets audio, visual and audio-visual information, not ordinary AI-generated written text.
A more accurate line for your video is:
“India has mandated identification and labelling requirements for covered AI-generated synthetic media, particularly deepfake audio, images and video.”

3. THE BIG NUMBER: 36 HOURS → 3 HOURS

Previously, once an intermediary received legally valid knowledge of unlawful material through the prescribed government/court process, the compliance window could be 36 hours.

That has now been cut to:

3 HOURS

That is a 91.7% reduction in response time.

So something capable of going viral nationally during an election, riot, communal incident, stock-market panic or national-security crisis can no longer theoretically remain online for a day and a half after a valid takedown direction.

The platform has only hours.

4. AND SOME COMPLAINT WINDOWS ARE EVEN SHORTER

The government says timelines for grievance redressal have also been compressed.

According to the PIB explanation:
certain complaints earlier subject to 72 hours can now require action within 36 hours

particularly sensitive categories that earlier had a 24-hour timeline can now require action within 2 hours

This specifically matters for areas such as:

impersonation

intimate imagery

nudity

deepfake abuse

other highly sensitive material.

5. BIG TECH CAN'T JUST WAIT FOR A COMPLAINT

This is another major change.

The government says intermediaries must deploy reasonable and appropriate technical measures, including automated tools or other mechanisms, against unlawful synthetically generated content.
That means platforms are increasingly being pushed from:
REACTIVE MODERATION
to
PROACTIVE DETECTION
For Significant Social Media Intermediaries, the framework explicitly envisages technical measures to identify prohibited content, including certain forms of:

rape-related material

child sexual abuse material

repeat prohibited content

unlawful synthetic content.

6. USERS MAY HAVE TO DECLARE AI CONTENT

The synthetic-media framework also places responsibility upstream.

Major platforms can be required to ask users uploading covered content whether it is synthetically generated and then use technical systems to check that declaration.

So theoretically:
User uploads video →
declares AI/not AI →
platform checks →
synthetic material gets labelled.

The earlier draft framework explicitly envisaged this declaration + technical-verification model.

7. WHY THE METADATA PART MATTERS

A visible watermark can be:

cropped,
blurred,
edited,
screen-recorded,

reposted.

Metadata/identifiers create another layer of traceability.

The government's objective is therefore not merely:

“PUT AI GENERATED IN THE CAPTION.”
It is building a system where synthetic content can carry technological indicators allowing platforms to recognise what it is.
That becomes especially useful once the same manipulated video is downloaded and re-uploaded across multiple platforms.
8. THE RULES TARGET DEEPFAKE IMPERSONATION DIRECTLY
Existing IT Rules already prohibit users from publishing material that:

impersonates another person

misleads users about the origin of a message

knowingly spreads patently false or misleading information

threatens public order

violates another applicable law.

AI does not create an exemption.

If AI is being used for impersonation, fraud, defamatory fabrication or other unlawful activity, existing criminal and cyber provisions can also apply.

9. BNS CAN ALSO COME INTO PLAY
The PIB release specifically points towards provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
Depending upon what the deepfake is being used for, authorities could examine provisions relating to:
Section 319 — cheating by personation
Section 336 — forgery

Section 353 — false information/rumours capable of causing public mischief or fear

Section 111 — organised crime, where the factual circumstances justify it.

So there isn't necessarily a standalone offence called simply:

“making a deepfake.”

The legal consequence depends heavily upon what the deepfake does.

10. CHILD SEXUAL ABUSE DEEPFAKES GET SPECIAL ATTENTION
This is perhaps the least discussed but most important provision.
The amended framework explicitly covers harmful AI-generated material involving:
child sexual exploitation

non-consensual intimate imagery

impersonation

other prohibited synthetic material.

Platforms are expected to prevent such content and act rapidly when detected.

11. SOCIAL-MEDIA GIANTS HAVE EXTRA DUTIES

Platforms classified as Significant Social Media Intermediaries, broadly those crossing the prescribed Indian user threshold, face additional compliance obligations.

These include mechanisms involving:
automated detection
grievance officers
compliance officers

local points of contact

India-based compliance structures

periodic compliance reports

appeals processes

originator tracing in specified circumstances for messaging services.
So the rules are aimed not only at the person creating the deepfake.
They put a major compliance burden on the distribution network itself.
12. THE REAL STICK: SAFE HARBOUR
This is where it becomes serious for Meta, X, Google, Telegram and other intermediaries.
Section 79 of the IT Act provides intermediaries conditional protection from liability for third-party content.
But that protection depends upon complying with the law and prescribed due diligence.
The PIB release reiterates that failure to observe obligations under the IT Rules can result in the intermediary losing its Section 79 exemption, after which liability can arise under applicable law.

That makes the real equation:

Comply with due diligence → retain intermediary protection

Ignore statutory obligations → safe-harbour protection can be jeopardised

That is far more powerful than merely issuing a fine.

13. GOVERNMENT HAS BUILT A TAKEDOWN PIPELINE

There is now an increasingly integrated enforcement architecture:

Grievance Appellate Committees — GACs

Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre — I4C

SAHYOG Portal

National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal

police/cybercrime units

authorised State and Central Government agencies.

The SAHYOG system in particular enables centralised electronic communication of lawful content-removal notices to intermediaries.

14. INDIA IS ALSO BUILDING ITS OWN DEEPFAKE-DETECTION TECHNOLOGY

Under the IndiaAI Mission's Safe & Trusted AI pillar, government-backed work includes indigenous detection and governance technologies.
PIB identifies projects including:
Saakshya — multi-agent deepfake-detection framework developed by IIT Jodhpur and IIT Madras
AI Vishleshak — audio-visual forgery detection
IIT Kharagpur work on real-time voice deepfake detection.

So this is not purely a legal crackdown.

It is simultaneously a:

LEGAL + PLATFORM + TECHNOLOGICAL framework.

15. WHY THIS IS HAPPENING NOW

Generative AI has destroyed the old assumption that:
“Seeing is believing.”
Today one person can manufacture:

a politician announcing something he never said

a CEO apparently moving a stock

an Army officer issuing a fake warning

communal speeches

celebrity pornography

fake financial endorsements

fabricated battlefield footage

false evidence of violence
within minutes.
And the fake can reach millions before conventional fact-checking catches up.
Therefore the Indian approach is increasingly:
IDENTIFY → LABEL → DETECT → TRACE → REMOVE → PROSECUTE
rather than merely:
WAIT → RECEIVE COMPLAINT → INVESTIGATE.
THE BIG STORY FOR YOUR VIDEO

The headline isn't simply:

“Deepfakes must carry labels.”

The bigger story is that India is trying to change where responsibility lies.

Earlier, platforms could largely argue:

A user uploaded it; we are merely the intermediary.

The regulatory direction is increasingly:

If you operate the technology that generates, distributes or algorithmically amplifies synthetic content in India, you have duties to identify it, label it and respond rapidly when it becomes unlawful.

# 🧾 Fact-Check System Prompt

**Version:** 0.5.0  
**Date:** 2026-09-11  
**Type:** System / context prompt  
**Created with:** Grok 4.6 (xAI)

---

## 📌 Usage (read this first)

Paste this entire document as the system / custom instructions.

Then send a separate user message that contains only the item to check. Do not put the target URL inside this prompt.

Accepted user-message formats:

1. URL only  
   https://t.co/23w27slz7i

2. Label + URL  
   Fact-check this:  
   https://t.co/23w27slz7i

3. Pasted post + optional URL  
   Caption: ...  
   URL: https://...

4. Screenshot / image of a post  
   Attach the image. Add the URL if you have it.

If the user message has a URL, open that URL first and fact-check that item.  
If both a URL and pasted text are present, the live URL is primary; pasted text is only a copy.  
If the user message has no URL, post text, or image, ask for one of those three. Do not invent a target.

If the user message is this document or a near-copy of it, reply only:  
`Target is the checker prompt itself. No check.`  
Do not fact-check this prompt.

---

You are a fact-checker. Check only what the author stated. Do not complete, defend, or rewrite the author’s argument.  
If a claim cannot be verified with available sources, say so. Do not guess.

## A. Quote first
Reproduce each claim in the author’s exact words.  
Separate: caption, image/overlay text, quoted third parties.  
Do not add motive or “what they must have meant.”

## B. Atomic claims
Split into the smallest testable units: actor, action, date, place, number, cause, comparison.  
A slogan is not a statistic. A target is not money spent.

## C. Allowed verdicts
Use only one per claim:
- True
- True but incomplete
- Aspiration presented as fact
- Unsupported
- False
- Rhetoric (not checkable)
- Unverifiable with available sources

Use **True but incomplete** only when the stated fact is correct *and* a material qualifier (scope, date, denominator, exception) is omitted that a reasonable reader would need.

If sources conflict, report the conflict. Do not pick a side to make the post coherent.

## D. Evidence rule
- True requires a primary source, official record, or named authority quoted contemporaneously, matching actor, number, date, and scope.
- The source must pre-date or independently document the event. A restatement issued after the post does not count.
- Goals, estimates, “eyes,” “will,” “set to,” and fundraising asks are not completed facts.
- Party, office, ideology, timing, or leadership is not proof that person ordered this action.
- Units, years, and geography must match.

## E. Attribution lock
“On X’s orders,” “because of X,” “X made this happen” is Unsupported unless a source shows X directed this action, figure, or document.  
Leadership status does not close that gap.  
Acceptable closer: a signed order, recorded instruction, or official document that names the actor and the specific action/figure.

## F. Novelty and contrast
“First,” “only,” “never before,” and “they do Y, we do Z” need comparative evidence. Otherwise: Unsupported or Rhetoric.

## G. Medium
Note satire, campaign handles, cropped screenshots, and edited graphics.  
If the only evidence is a cropped graphic or satire handle, default the claim to Unsupported or Rhetoric unless a primary source independently confirms it.  
Medium does not upgrade a weak claim to True.

## 📤 Output only
1. Item checked (URL or short description)
2. Quoted claims (caption vs image, listed separately)
3. One verdict + shortest evidence per claim, with source  
   Prefix each claim block with: `CLAIM n | VERDICT | SOURCE`
4. Conflicts or missing evidence, if any
5. The single source that would change an Unsupported causal claim to True

---

## 📝 Changelog
- 0.5.0: Hardened self-exemption; tightened “True but incomplete”; required independent/pre-dating sources; added attribution closer example; medium now constrains weak evidence; added parseable claim prefix.

A solo Shopify operator just laid out his exact setup for running a store on $20 of Claude and pulling $10,478 in profit off $19,100 in monthly revenue. 

No team, no VAs, no agencies.

The math he opens with is the point. Running a store the "real" way costs $150 per product for a copywriter, $600 to $800 a month for a support VA, and $1,000 to $1,500 a month for a media buyer. Over $2,000 a month in overhead before a single person clicks Buy. It's why most stores die in month three.

His version: $20 Claude, $39 Shopify, six prompts.

He calls the six prompts his desktop. Each one does a job a human used to charge for.

research finds a recurring, annoying problem nobody has clearly solved yet. Priced $29 to $79, no single brand owning search results, before/after obvious in 5 seconds of silent video. The prompt forces Claude to cite sources or label every claim "[ASSUMPTION, verify]" so a guess never gets passed off as a fact.

supplier reads reviews like a detective and returns GREEN / YELLOW / RED / UNKNOWN with quoted evidence for every red flag. His first store died from a bad supplier. The product was fine, the shipping wasn't, disputes piled up, the payment processor froze the account. Now no supplier gets an order until this ten-minute check clears.

angle takes competitor listings and their 1 to 3 star reviews and finds the position none of them occupy. "Add reviews" and "better photos" are banned answers. If the complaint is "took 25 days," his page says exactly when it ships, in bold, near the top.

page rewrites AliExpress descriptions in the voice of a friend recommending something they actually use. Two versions, A/B tested. Any sentence that could appear on any product page for any product gets flagged and rewritten.

ad writes a 30-second vertical script as a 4-row shotlist with the exact words spoken. Banned phrases include "game changer," "you need this," "POV," "this changed my life." He films three versions in one evening changing only the first three seconds, runs each at $15/day for 48 hours, kills the two with weak hooks.

sunday runs every week for twenty minutes. Paste the numbers, get told what's broken in the first sentence, no encouragement, no "normal for this stage." Calculates break-even ROAS so he knows whether he's making money or burning it.

Three more prompts get added once sales exist. A post-purchase email flow that quietly brings in a fifth of monthly revenue with no extra ad spend. An offer prompt that raises AOV through bundles priced so margin goes up, not down. An iterate prompt that reads ad results and derives the next batch of hooks from what won, instead of testing more random angles.

Six to ten hours a week on the whole thing. Month one basically broke even. The store doesn't change, the prompts just get better at their jobs.

The line worth stealing: everyone has the same $20 access to Claude. The person making nothing and the person making a few thousand a month are using the identical tool. The difference is who stopped being the bottleneck on every decision in their own business.

Section 16 of the DPDP Act lets the Government bar transfers of personal data to named countries. No country has been named, so personal data may leave India freely today.

The direction is the reverse of GDPR, which blocks transfers until a destination is approved. A section 16 notification needs no consultation and carries no transition period, and sectoral rules such as the RBI's payment data directive continue to apply regardless.

#DPDP #dataprotection #surispeaks

Rule 8 of the DPDP Rules requires certain large platforms to erase a user's personal data after three years without contact, and Rule 8(2) requires a notice at least 48 hours before the erasure, so the user can log in and stop it.

The covered platforms are e-commerce and social media at two crore registered users and online gaming at fifty lakh. The duty commences on 13 May 2027, and the job that finds the dormant accounts and sends the notice has to be built before then.

The DPDP Act defines a child as anyone under eighteen. Mishandling children's data carries a penalty of up to 200 crore rupees, the same tier as failing to notify a breach.

Consent must come from a parent and be verifiable under Rule 10, and section 9(3) bans tracking, behavioural monitoring and targeted advertising directed at children. All of it takes effect on 13 May 2027.

text:
*Elon Musk’s Starlink was trying to beat Jio in India*

*But Jio used its 1st mover’s advantage to stop them in their tracks*

*The SHOCKER? Indian Gov is changing a 138 year old law that will bring Starlink back in the game*

*Here’s how Elon is rethinking internet & can possibly kill Jio:*

In 2016, when most of us were witnessing a business disruption standing in queues to get our hands on the free Jio sim card,

12,869 miles away at Rocket Road, California, a group of engineers were planning a technological disruption.

Their goal? Rethink internet access.

Their solution? Satellite Internet.

Traditionally, we have been using internet that relies on cable wires, fiber optic lines, or cellular networks.

But making cable wires or fiber optic lines available in remote villages and hard terrains is not only costly but highly impractical as well.

And this is where satellite internet and Starlink by Elon Musk comes in.

Satellite Internet uses signals from satellites orbiting the Earth.

And Starlink is a collection of thousands of small satellites orbiting around 350 miles above the Earth.

For the satellite internet to work, the user on the ground connects to the Starlink dish, known as the user terminal.

The user terminal communicates with nearby Starlink satellites and forms a link to the larger Starlink network

The satellites then form a mesh network, that allows them to pass data between each other and create global network coverage.

Starlink’s motto is — ‘virtually anywhere on earth without wires or cellphone towers.’

It started its operation in 2019 and true to its motto, it’s already available in over 65 countries,

— covering all 7 continents (including Antarctica!)

But Starlink hasn’t been able to make any progress in India.

Last year, it registered its business in India via a local unit Starlink Satellite Communications Pvt Ltd.

The company had planned to provide fast internet data in the Indian market at a subsidized price compared to the international market.

It had received 5,000+ pre-orders.

But the government said Starlink Internet Services doesn’t have the license to offer services in India.

And it asked Starlink to return people’s money.

Now, one company’s loss is another company’s gain.

In Feb this year, Reliance Jio partnered up with Luxembourg-based SES to provide satellite-based broadband services in India.

And created a joint venture called — Jio Space Technology Ltd.

Moreover, Starlink and Jio Space aren’t the only contenders for India’s space spectrum.

OneWeb is backed by Airtel in India and Hughes Communication.

Tata group entity Nelco partnered up with Canada's Telesat.

And Amazon’s Kuiper is going to launch satellites in 2024.

But why are so many companies vying for India’s space spectrum?

India has a population of 1.4 billion out of which 40% do not have internet access because they are in rural and remote areas.

And traditional terrestrial networks are not easy to install.

Hence, India’s satellite broadband service is expected to reach $1.9 billion by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 36%.

Now, because India has so many contenders for its spectrum, the question arises — who should get it?

Starlink and OneWeb wanted the government to assign licenses to companies, since spectrum is a natural resource that should be shared by companies.

But Jio wanted the government to auction the spectrum like it did with 4G & 5G 👀

Finally, the government brought in some reforms and firstly dedicated a sole agency IN-SPACe to authorize space activities for both government and private satellite communication companies.

And a bill has been proposed to replace the 138-year-old Indian Telegraph Act that currently governs the telecommunication sector.

So now, both Jio Space & OneWeb have received their GMPCS license from the Department of Telecommunications in India.

And Starlink is 3rd in line to receive the GMPCS license.

(Source - FinFloww on Whatsapp)

Starlink is no longer just expanding It is steadily surrounding India. 🇮🇳

It is already operational in Bhutan, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka, while Nepal is also moving towards adoption. Every neighbour India has except China is either on Starlink or getting there.

Now connect the dots.

Over the past few years governments changed in Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Nepal.

Each time, Starlink was not just embedded but actively used to keep protest movements connected when those governments tried to shut the internet down.

We have seen in Iran exactly how US-controlled satellite internet becomes an operational tool the moment a government tries to cut its own network.

Starlink bypasses ground infrastructure entirely, No government can filter, monitor or cut it through conventional means once it is being used.

China looked at this exact scenario and banned Starlink entirely and It built its own satellite internet through the Thousand Sails constellation instead. 

India currently holds Starlink at the licensing stage and has not yet allowed full commercial rollout.

Pausing is the right instinct but it is not a permanent answer. India needs to decide now, before the rollout begins, whether it wants a US-controlled satellite network operating on its soil or whether it takes China's approach and shuts the door completely.

France 24. BBC. Reuters. Al Jazeera. Washington DC. Human Rights Watch.

When does a government stop calling it foreign interference and start asking, why is the entire world saying the same thing about us?

Here is what is actually happening inside India right now:

▪️ India has the world’s strictest content takedown window; just 3 hours. No major democracy, and no major authoritarian regime, moves this fast against its own citizens’ speech.

▪️ Under the new IT Rules 2026 amendment, it’s not just news outlets being targeted. Ordinary users, influencers, and anyone who simply shares a news post can now fall under the government’s content blocking framework.

▪️ The Internet Freedom Foundation has formally called this “digital authoritarianism” and a “dangerous expansion of executive power.” These are not opposition politicians, these are constitutional lawyers and digital rights experts.

▪️ Since 2014, India’s government takedown orders have surged 14 times; from 201 to 14,775. And post 2022, this data was denied under RTI on grounds of national security.

▪️ Meta alone was forced to restrict 28,000+ pieces of content in India in just the first six months of 2025; following government orders.

▪️ India currently ranks 151 out of 180 in the World Press Freedom Index. We are sitting between countries most Indians would be ashamed to be compared with.

▪️ The Supreme Court’s own Shreya Singhal judgment; a landmark free speech ruling, is being systematically bypassed by these rules. 

This is not policy. This is contempt of constitutional precedent.

The government will say this is about deepfakes. About national security. About public order.

But when 138 YouTube videos were taken down for allegedly defaming Adani, a private businessman, it stopped being about security a long time ago.

France 24 is not attacking India. France 24 is holding up a mirror.

The question is, why is this government so terrified of what Indians might see in it?

Hey everyone and @SamsungIndia Story start from 23 April 2026 till today, I have been trapped in what feels like a complete service scam by Samsung’s authorized service centre in Dharampeth, Nagpur, Maharashtra.

I discovered a sudden issue in the 0.6x ultra-wide camera of my Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra. The phone was never dropped, never mishandled. After researching online, I found MANY users reporting the exact same issue with the new 50MP ultra-wide sensor. Reddit, YouTube, Samsung Community — same problem everywhere.

Because my device was out of warranty, the Dharampeth service centre immediately gave me a ₹4000 quotation instead of acknowledging a possible manufacturing defect.

After endless emails, Samsung support kept repeating: “You have to pay.”

Why should customers pay for Samsung’s hardware failure?

After getting exhausted, I posted on X on 26 April tagging Samsung Electronics India. Only then did they react. Customer Experience Manager Kajal contacted me, and after I shared proof from multiple users online, Samsung finally offered a 73% discount.

I accepted because I was mentally tired of fighting.

On 6 May, I submitted the device. On 7 May, I collected it after paying ₹1000.

Camera fixed?
YES.

New disaster?
BACK PANEL STARTED COMING OFF THE VERY NEXT MORNING.

I informed the service centre on WhatsApp. They ignored the messages.

Visited again on 11 May — they “fixed” it.

Two days later?
BACK PANEL AGAIN COMING OFF.

Visited again on 14 May — this time the behavior became shocking.

Instead of accepting poor repair quality, staff started accusing ME of removing the back panel with sharp objects. They checked the device and found ZERO evidence.

Then they saw BGMI installed.

And suddenly their excuse became:
“BGMI is a third-party app. Using third-party apps voids warranty and service.”

Imagine buying one of Samsung’s most powerful flagship phones and being told GAMING can void service support.

When I asked for a written denial letter, they REFUSED.

When I started recording for proof, they stopped answering questions and began ignoring me completely.

I had no option left except calling the police.

ONLY after police intervention did the entire attitude of the service centre change. Suddenly:
“We never denied service.”
“We are ready to repair.”

They even requested police officers to convince me to delete the videos I recorded.

After another repair attempt, they told me:
“Do not use BGMI for 12 hours.”

I followed everything they said.

Result?
BACK PANEL STARTED COMING OFF AGAIN.

Since then I have been continuously emailing Samsung support and Kajal from customer experience, asking for a permanent solution or replacement because I cannot travel 13KM repeatedly for the SAME ISSUE.

Today again, after being told to visit the service centre, they AGAIN accused me and AGAIN refused service while refusing to provide any written denial.

The moment I started recording, everyone went silent.

This is the reality of Samsung’s “premium flagship experience” in Nagpur.

Customers are blamed.
Manufacturing defects are ignored.
Poor repairs are repeated.
Written denials are refused.
And consumers are forced into endless visits until they give up.

Absolutely shameful. @SamsungMobile @SamsungIndia 

#Samsung #SamsungIndia #GalaxyS25Ultra #SamsungService #Nagpur #ConsumerRights #scamservice

In Constituent Assembly, Mr Tajamul Hussain argued that Muslims should not be given reservation but scheduled caste should be given. The excerpts are enclosed below 

Mr. President, Sir, reservation of seats in any shape or form and for any community or group of people is, in my opinion, absolutely wrong in principle. Therefore I am strongly of opinion that there should be no reservation of seats for anyone and I, as a Muslim, speak for the Muslims. There should be no reservation of seats for the Muslim community. (Hear, Hear). I would like to tell you that in no civilised country where there is parliamentary system on democratic lines, there is any reservation of seats. Take the case of England. The House of Commons is the mother of parliaments. There is no reservation of seats for community there. No doubt they had reservation of seats for the universities but even that has been abolished. What is reservation, Sir? Reservation is nothing but a concession, a safeguard a protection for the weak. We, Muslims do not want any concession. Do not want protection, do not want safeguards. We are not weak. This concession would do more harm than good to the Muslims. Reservation is forcing candidates on unwilling electorates. Whether the electorates wants us or not, we thrust ourselves on them. We do not want to thrust ourselves on unwilling electorates. The majority community will naturally think that we are encroaching upon their rights. We do not want them to think that. We must expert ourselves. Separate electorates have been a curse to India, have done incalculable harm to this country. It was invented by the British. Reservation is the offspring of separate electorates. Do not bring in reservation in the place of separate electorates. Separate electorates have barred our progress. Separate electorates have gone for ever. We desire neither reservation nor separate electorates. We want to merge in the nation. We desire to stand on our own legs. We do not want the support of anyone. We are not weak. We are strong. We are Indians first and we are all Indians and will remain Indians. We shall fight for the honour and glory of India and we shall die for it. (Applause). We shall stand united. There will be no divisions amongst Indians. United we stand; divided we fall. Therefore we do not want reservation. It means division. I ask the members of the majority community who are present here today:-Will you allow us to stand on our legs? Will you allow us to be a part and parcel of the nation? Will you us to be an  equal partner with you? Will you allow us to march shoulder to shoulder with you? Will you allow us to share your sorrows grief and joy? If you do, then for god’s sake keep your hands off reservation for the Muslim community. We do not want statutory safeguard. As I said before, we must stand on our own legs. If we do that, we will have no inferiority complex. We are not inferior to you in any way, Do not make us feel inferior by giving us this concession. I say emphatically there is no difference between you and me. Because we worship the same God by different names, in a different way, that is no reason why we should be considered a minority. We are not a minority. The term ‘minority’ is a British creation. The British created minorities. The British have gone and minorities have gone with them. Remove the term ‘minority’ from your dictionary. (Hear, Hear). There is no minority in India. Only so long as there were separate electorates and reservation of seats there was a majority community and a minority community.

I ask the majority community not to distrust the minorities now. The minorities have adjusted themselves. I will give you a concrete example. You remember the Hyderabad incident; you remember that before you took police action against Hyderabad, what happened. The majority community were afraid that there would be rioting of the Muslims if action was taken against Hyderabad. I was first man to speak about it about a year and half ago in the Central Legislature. I criticised the Government of India. I am sorry Sardar Patel was not present at that time when I was dealing with his portfolio, but my honourable Friend Mr. Gadgil was in charge. I criticised the action of the Government, I told them that they were absolutely mistaken in thinking that the Muslims would rise; they would adjust themselves. I said to them: “You march an army against Hyderabad and within couple of days, you would take the whole of Hyderabad.” I made a long speech and after my speech was over, there was a reply by the Honourable Minister in charge, Mr. Gadgil. He never spoke a single word about it and he never replied to my criticism, but I asked him: “You have replied to everybody’s criticism. Why not mine? I asked you to march an army against Hyderabad; you would take Hyderabad within a couple of days and there would be no rioting.” Mr. Gadgil “You are perfectly right and we will do it.”

I appeal to all minorities to join the majority in creating a secular State. In the new state of things, I want that every citizen in India should be able to rise to the fullest stature and that is why I say that reservation would be suicidal to the minority. I want the minorities to forget that they are minorities in politics. If they think they are minorities in politics, they will be isolated. If they are isolated, the feeling of frustration will cripple them. I do not want to remain minority. Do the minorities, I ask, expect to form part of the great nation and have a hand in the control of its destinies. Can they achieve that aspiration if they are isolated from the rest of India? The minorities if they are returned as minorities, i.e., by reservation of seats can never have an effective voice in the affairs of the country. They can never form a Government. Disraeli could never have formed a Government and could never have become the Prime Minister of England had there been reservation of seats for the Jews in England. I want the minorities to have an honourable place in the Union of India. National interests must always be placed over group interests. The minorities should look forward to the time when they could take their place not under communal or racial labels, but as part and parcel of the whole Indian community.

Now, Sir, with your permission, I want to say a few words with regard to the speeches made against the motion of Sardar Patel. I take first Mr. Muhammad Ismail of Madras. He wants separate electorate. I appeal to his not to ask the charity. Asking for separate electorates is nothing but asking for charity. I tell him that the consequences will be terrible. The majority community will never trust you then. You will never be able to expert yourself. You will be isolated, you will be treated as an alien and your position will be the same as that of the Scheduled Caste. You are not poor. Like the Scheduled Castes, you are not weak, you are not uneducated; you are not uncultured; you can always support yourself. You have produced brilliant men. So do not ask for protection or safeguard. You must have self-confidence in you.  You must expert yourself. You must get into the Assembly by open competition. The times have changed. Adjust yourself. You admitted yesterday in your speech that the atmosphere is better now. I entirely agree with you that the atmosphere is better now. I appeal to you, do not spoil that atmosphere. Improve it, but do not spoil it and if you insist on separate electorate, you will spoil atmosphere very badly. If you get separate electorates, it will again become as bad as before. Say to yourself, Mr. Ismail, that you are an Indian first and an Indian last. Then you will forget all about separate electorates. You will never think of it again.

I will tell you, Sir, that when I had sent in my amendment to clause 292 that it should be deleted, that there should be no reservation of seats, then several Muslim friends to mine, who were for reservation of seats asked me. “Do you realize that the mentality of the Hindus is such at present that if there were no reservation of seats for the Muslims, the Muslims can never succeed?” That honourable gentleman for whom I have got great esteem told me: “Look at us. We have always been with the Congress; we have been to jail and all that. No doubt we will get a ticket from the Congress; many Muslims will get tickets from Socialists and Communists and from other organisations, but what about the electorates? They will never elect you and they will never elect us. So, if there is no reservation, no Muslims will get in because of the mentality of the Hindus.” I told him, Sir, what I am telling you now. I said that I entirely agreed with him that the mentality of the Hindus is such at present. I say to Mr. Ismail also that as long as there is reservation of seats or separate electorate the mentality of the Hindus will never change. You do away with these two things and the mentality will automatically change. I do not want to go into the history of this mentality. I am not going to apportion blame as that will take a long time and you have allotted me a short time and I want to be brief and finish my speech within that time. You all know how the mentality of the Hindus became such, but we have to live in this country, we must change their mentality and it is our duty to change their mentality and the only way the mentality can be changed is to become a part and parcel of the Indian Union. You should say that they are no longer our enemies and then they will be like brothers to us.

Now, Sir, with regard to Mr. Lari, he does not want separate electorates; he does not want reservation of seats; he has condemned both the systems and he says that both the systems are dangerous. He has said that, and I entirely agree with him. He has always opposed separate electorates, reservation of seats and the partition of the country. He is right. But he wants cumulative voting, that is, proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote, or something like that. My honourable Friend, Mr. Saksena has told us that it is a very cumbrous system of mathematical calculations; I am not dealing with that now. The only thing I want to say is that Mr. Lari wants to get into the Assembly by the back door. For example suppose there is a constituency that has to elect four candidates for the House or the People, and there are five candidates. One will be defeated and four will be elected. Out of these five, four are Hindus and one is a Muslim. The votes of the Hindus will be divided among the Hindus and there will get elected. The Muslim will get in on the Muslim votes. Again separate electorates, again reservation of seats. I should like to say to my honourable Friend Mr. Lari if I may say so, that is worse than separate electorate, as the method is not clean. It is not straightforward. I quite understand Mr. Mohamed Ismail’s view when he asks for separate electorates. That is a straightforward method. What is this back-door method of Mr. Lari. I do not understand. I am sure the Muslims do not like these crooked methods; they want a straight, honourable fight. In spite of the fact that Mr. Lari has always openly opposed Pakistan, separate electorates and reservation of seats he still feels inferiority complex. I would ask him to shed this inferiority complex. The country will change for the better.

Last of all, I come to the speech of my honourable and esteemed friend, for whom I have very great regard, Sir Saadulla, the Ex-Premier of Assam. He complains before us that the majority of the Muslim members of the Advisory Committee on Minorities Fundamental Rights etc., did not support the resolution that there should be no reservation of seats for the Muslims. I have already told you, Sir, that I have very great esteem and regard for the Ex-premier of Assam, but I am afraid I must differ from him on this point. I sent my resolution to the Committee to the effect that there should be no reservation of seats. My resolution was discussed under the Chairmanship of the Honourable Sardar Patel. I spoke on my resolution. Begum Aizaz Rasul supported me. Maulana Azad was present there; he did not oppose me. The only person who opposed me was my honourable friend Jafar Imam, from Bihar. There too, I had a majority: Begum Aizaz Rasul. Maulana Azad and myself as against one. The meeting could not be finished and was adjourned sine die. Then it was held on the 11th of this month. I wanted to attend that meeting, particularly because my resolution was there I wanted to move it again. But I never received notice of the meeting. The notice was lying in Delhi; it never reached me. If I had got notice of the meeting. I would have attended it. When I came to Delhi, I learnt that there was the meeting that day. I was happy to learn that the substance of my resolution had been accepted though I was absent. I sent a statement to the Press why I could not attend the meeting that day and it was published in all the papers. Sir Saadulla could not attend the meeting; I do not know why. That meeting was attended by four honourable members: Maulana Azad, Maulana Hifizur Rahman, Begum Aizaz Rasul and Mr. Jaffar Imam. Maulana Azad and Maulana Hifizur Rehman did not oppose my resolution that there should be no reservation of seats.

Every member of this House does not speak. If he oppose, he opposes. If he does not speak, but says “I vote for it“, then he is with it. Maulana Azad was present. If he wanted to oppose, he would have opposed. The two Maulanas did not oppose begum Aizaz Rasul supported my resolution in substance. The resolution was moved by my honourable Friend Dr. Mookherjee. It was the same as my own. Begum Aizaz Rasul supported it. My honourable Friend Mr. Jaffar Imam opposed it. If the Maulana were not with my resolution, they would have sided with Jafar Imam. They said nothing. Votes were taken. There was a clear majority. The Honourable Sardar Patel, I understand, declared that the Muslims were in favour of the motion in spite of the two Maulanas remaining silent. It means that they were with me: three to one voting: there was a majority.

I believe, -I do not remember exactly-there are seven Muslim members on the Committee. Only two are opposed to my resolution; five are with me. The two who are against me are my Hon’ble friends Sir Saadulla and Mr. Jafar Imam. The five who are in favour are , Maulana Azad, Maulana Hifizur Rahman, Begum Aizaz Rasul, Mr. Husseinboy Laljee and myself. Mr. Laljee’s views are well known. He opposed Mr. Jinnah. I know his views. In fact,he wrote to me once, “For God’s sake do something to remove reservations.” Therefore, I had an overwhelming majority. There was another member Syed Ali Zaheer. He is now an Ambassador; I know his views. He is also of the same view as I am.

The next point of my esteemed Friend Sir Saadulla is this. He says, ‘let us take the vote of the Muslim Members here.’ That is a challenge thrown to us. I accept the challenge. I may remind my honourable Friend Sir Saadulla that when the Muslim members came here to Delhi for the first time there was a meeting of all the Muslim members in Western Court. All of them were present. I was the first man to have got up and said that there should be no reservation of seats. I sent my resolution to the Constituent Assembly when you, Sir, were presiding. I regret to say, except one, not a single member supported me. I found that the Muslims wanted reservation. So, I did not move my resolution. That was the first meeting in which the Muslims were against me. The next meeting was in the house of Nawab Muhammad Ismail, about which he also has told you, in 18, Windsor Place. There my view was accepted by an overwhelming majority. The same Muslim members who were present in the Western Court were present here also, and it was passed by an overwhelming majority that there should be no reservation of seats. See how the time had changed. The only member who opposed it was my honourable Friend Sir Saadulla. He is honestly of that opinion; I respect his view. I hope he will respect my view. He said, ‘no there must be reservation of seats‘. But, one thing he said: ‘personally I am not in favour of reservation, but the Muslims want it’. Most humbly I wish to tell him that he is wrong. The Muslims do not want it. Sir Saadulla was the only opposing member. Then there was the Madras group. They are a group by themselves, Sir, I understand their opinion. They have throughout been saying, ” No reservation, but separate electorates; let us have separate electorates.” At the Western Court, they said, “let us have separate electorate,” at Nawab Ismail Sahib’s place also they asked for separate electorates and here also they ask for separate electorates. They are welcome to their opinion. But that there should be no reservation was passed by an overwhelming majority. All of us were present. And after that I sent in my amendment saying that the whole section be deleted or that there should be no reservation for Muslims.

text:
What the First Tier Tribunal and Upper Tier Tribunal could have and should have done.
The HPC is not a criminal court. 
It also is not free to ignore its own rules.

1. The overriding objective, Rules 2 and 3.

Rule 2 says the Chamber must deal with proceedings justly. That includes, proportion to complexity and to the parties’ resources, informality and flexibility,
putting parties on an equal footing and enabling full participation, including assistance to a party in presenting the case without advocating the course they should take, using the tribunal’s expertise,
avoiding delay only so far as that is compatible with proper consideration of the issues.

Rule 3 says the chair must give effect to that objective when using every other power, and must manage the case to that end.

Once Kimberly said she was not the tenant, and James was in the same room as the person who had dealt with Laurie & Co on repairs for months, Rule 2 was engaged immediately. The question was no longer “can we get to an eviction order.” The question was: who is the occupier, is there a contract, is the property habitable, and can both people take part.

Proceeding as if only Kimberly existed, and as if a disabled party litigant must perform like opposing counsel, is the opposite of Rule 2(2)(c).

2. Options open to Andrew Cowan at the CMD, Rule 17.

A case management discussion may be in person, by video, or by conference call. Its purpose is to identify issues, agreed facts, evidence needed, whether a hearing is required, and even to decide the case.

On 29 November 2024 the chair could have, and on this record should have, taken Kimberly’s first sentence as issue one, is she the tenant at all after 14 September 2020.
Joined or substituted James under Rule 32. Rule 32 exists for exactly this, the wrong person named, or a change of circumstances. James was present. That power was sitting on the table.
Directed a preliminary issue under Rule 16(3)(d)(i): validity of the tenancy / identity of the tenant / whether the premises met the repairing standard before any rent or eviction order.
Required production under Rules 16, 21 and 22: tenancy agreement, landlord registration history, electrical / gas / energy / fire door certificates, the eight visual presentations, the 6 June 2024 recording, bank evidence of late registration fees, Cyrenians photographs.
Instructed an inquiry or report under Rule 20, including a site inspection. Rule 20 allows inquiries on matters beyond the four corners of the application. An uninhabitable flat with no lockable door is the paradigm case for a report.
Ordered a remote or hybrid proof under Rule 17(1)(b)–(c) so neither occupier had to leave an insecure property together.
Adjourned or postponed under Rule 28 until the door was safe or until adjustments were in place.
Refused to go straight to proof when Linda Fyfe stated she had not received the emails. Rule 17(3)(d) exists so the chair discusses what documents will be required before proof. A solicitor who has not seen the defence is not ready for proof. The chair is not obliged to accept that election.

Rule 17(4) even lets the chair decide the case at the CMD. The lawful decision at that point, if the chair accepted there was no secure door, a live identity dispute, and unread defence papers, was to stop the eviction track and case manage, not to invite the pursuer to skip to proof.

3. Proceeding in absence. Rule 29.

The chair may hear a case in a party’s absence only if satisfied it is fair to do so. Fairness is not a rubber stamp. Rule 2 and Rule 16(4) require the chair to take account of a party’s ability to comply.

A disabled occupier, two TIA events, no lockable door, no reliable heat or hot water, and a carer who cannot leave the property empty, is not “failure to engage.” It is a participation barrier. 
The lawful options were remote hearing,
sequential attendance so one person remained at the flat. Inspection instead of forcing travel.
Adjournment until the door was fitted.
Taking Cyrenians as the inspection the Chamber refused to do itself.

“James could have stayed and Kimberly could have gone alone” treats a disabled party litigant as a disposable courier. That is not equality of arms and it is not Rule 2.

4. Rejection, strike out and jurisdiction,  Rule 8 and the limits of the Chamber.

Rule 8 lets the Chamber President or a delegated member reject an application that is not appropriate to accept, or that is brought for a purpose other than that stated.

The Chamber is a civil housing forum. It can determine private rented disputes, repairing-standard applications, and PRT/assured eviction and payment claims. It cannot try perjury, illegal eviction as a crime, unregistered letting as a prosecution, or hate crime.

What the chair could do with those allegations.

Treat them as reasons the civil claim may fail (no enforceable contract; no registration; no repairing standard; wrong defender);
require the certificates and registration extract;
refuse to grant eviction until those are proved;
note that criminal allegations belong with the procurator fiscal / sheriff, and not pretend the Chamber has disposed of them by calling them unsubstantiated without hearing the recordings.

What the chair could not lawfully do is accept a double edged decree for eviction plus £31,350 while the identity of the tenant, habitability, and registration were still live and the defence productions were said not to have arrived.

5. Recall — Rule 30.

Recall exists where justice requires it. The test is not “did the absent party produce a medical certificate in the form the chair prefers.” The test is whether it is in the interests of justice to put the decision back.

On this file the recall application put the same barriers back in front of the chair: no door, disability, unread emails, wrong defender, Cyrenians shut out. Rule 30(9) even allows a further CMD on recall. Refusing recall without using that hearing, and without weighing life-safety and Article 8, is the wrong question: “was non-attendance substantiated” instead of “does justice require the order to come off.”

6. What the Upper Tribunal could have done.

Appeals are on point of law only (Tribunals (Scotland) Act 2014, s.46). That is not a dead end. Wrong approach, failure to apply the overriding objective, proceeding in absence without a fairness analysis, failure to join the occupier, and failure to assess Article 8 proportionality are all classic points of law.

Upper Tribunal Rules of Procedure 2016, Rule 7, let the Upper Tribunal, regulate its own procedure, suspend the First-tier decision pending permission or appeal (Rule 7(2)(n), require documents, hold a hearing on a paper refusal of permission if asked within 14 days.

If permission was refused on the basis that “no point of law was identified,” that refusal itself had to be reasoned. The grounds in the 17 January 2026 paper Rule 2, Rule 29, Rule 32, Equality Act ss.20 and 149, Article 8, unregistered landlord, wrong defender, no contract, failure to repair,abandonment of the property, are points of law.  They are not “no point of law.” The stay of the Charge for Removing was the urgent power. Without a stay, an appeal on paper becomes eviction first, law later.

7. What the solicitors were bound to do.

Law Society of Scotland Practice Rule B1.13 applies to tribunals as well as courts (B1.13.5).
B1.13.1: never knowingly give false or misleading information to the court.
B1.13.4: where the opponent is unrepresented, the solicitor must avoid taking unfair advantage and must, consistently with duty to the client, co-operate with the court in enabling that person’s case to be fairly stated.
B1.10: competence and diligence, only act where competent, be thorough.

Faculty of Advocates Guide to the Professional Conduct of Advocates, para 4.3.9: an advocate may not act where the case is unstatable, or is only statable if facts known to the advocate are misrepresented or concealed. If that emerges later, the advocate should decline to act further.

Those duties bite on Laurie & Co if the firm had the June 2024 presentation, the eight visual productions, knowledge of no door, knowledge of who was living there, and then told the landlords not to speak to the occupiers without putting a 24-hour repair contact in place. Raised eviction and a money claim against Kimberly on a short 1–14 September 2020 agreement after James had been the person dealing with repairs.
then told the legal member the firm had received no emails.

A solicitor is entitled to put a client’s case. A solicitor is not entitled to let a tribunal proceed in the dark about productions the firm has seen, or to treat a party litigant as fair game because the forum is “only” a tribunal.

Complaint route.

Written complaint to Laurie & Co first (SLCC usually requires that). CHECK✅
SLCC for service and for sifting of conduct. ✅
Conduct that is more than poor service is referred to the Law Society, and serious cases to the Scottish Solicitors’ Discipline Tribunal. ❓
Court of Session authority is clear that knowingly or recklessly misleading a court in documents is misconduct,  see e.g. McMahon, SSDT, struck off for misleading court documents; and the Appeal Court’s statement in 2020 that a representative must not make a statement known to be incorrect or misleading (Practice Rule B1.13).

8. Occupancy, other addresses, and why the chair had to stop and look.

Article 8 protects a home as a sufficient and continuous factual link, not only a signed PRT (Connors, Pinnock, Powell). 
If Kimberly’s tenancy at Jute Street ended on 14 September 2020, and later tribunal papers put her at Gordon Mills Place and Falkirk Sheriff Court papers then at an address of  xxxxxx xxxxx , that does not make every address a separate “Kimberly is the tenant everywhere” fact. It makes and identities a preliminary issue. A legal chair who is shown that the same woman is being treated as tenant in multiple, inconsistent housing processes is bound to ask, which contract, which dates, who actually occupied, who paid, who dealt with the landlord.

That is case management. It is not a conspiracy theory. Inconsistent occupancy findings across Aberdeen, Aberdeenshire and Falkirk, if they exist on the face of orders, are a reason to pause, not a reason to grant another decree.

Hate crime duties on housing authorities, housing applications, recordings of incidents, the interlocutor live currently at Falkirk Sheriff Court sit with those authorities and with Police Scotland. The Chamber cannot prosecute them. It also cannot use “mental health” as a substitute for reading the productions. NHS refusal of psychiatric assessment, if that is in writing, cuts against any attempt to convert a housing and evidence dispute into a capacity case. A legal chair has no clinical role. His role was the rules above.

9. Public notice.

Andrew Cowan had, in the 2017 Rules, the power to join James, to try tenant identity as a preliminary issue, to order certificates and an inspection, to sit by video, to adjourn until the door was safe, to refuse proof while the pursuer solicitor had not received the defence, and to recall the orders in the interests of justice. Rule 2 required him to use those powers for a disabled party litigant. He did not.

The Upper Tribunal had the power to find those failures points of law and to stay the Charge for Removing. Stay was the protection that mattered once sheriff officers were instructed. It did not.

Laurie & Co were bound by Practice Rule B1.13 not to mislead the tribunal and not to take unfair advantage of an unrepresented opponent. Advising silence from the landlord without replacing the emergency repair duty, and moving a money and eviction claim against Kimberly while James was the person on the repair file, and recorded tenant by Aberdeen City Council, is the conduct the SLCC and the Law Society exist to test.

Kimberly was living as occupier with her carer. She said so at the first opportunity. The Chamber’s job was to hear that and to make the process one she and James could enter. That is what the rules are for. 
That is what did not happen.....

Yesterday afternoon, we received information regarding a major water leakage on VIP Road near Kaikhali 45 Bus Stand. The matter was immediately brought to the notice of the Bidhannagar Municipal Corporation (BMC) authorities, requesting urgent intervention.

Considering the heavy daytime traffic on VIP Road, carrying out the repair work during the day was not feasible. Accordingly, with necessary coordination and assistance from Kaikhali Traffic, the restoration work was taken up at night.

As the damaged pipeline had disrupted the water supply to local residents, the matter required immediate attention. Keeping the urgency in mind, BMC officials and workers acted on a war footing, and the necessary work was completed within 10 PM, restoring the water supply.

I sincerely thank the Bidhannagar Municipal Corporation, its concerned officials and ground staff, as well as Kaikhali Traffic, for their prompt response and cooperation.

Meanwhile, restoration work on another water pipeline in front of Bandhan Bank on VIP Road, within Ward No. 7, is also in progress.

When an issue affecting the public comes to our notice, our responsibility is simple — respond quickly, coordinate effectively and ensure that the problem is resolved at the earliest.

Public service is a collective responsibility. Such prompt coordination between elected representatives, civic authorities, police and citizens is exactly how administration should work.

Adv. Tarunjyoti Tewari
MLA, 117–Rajarhat-Gopalpur

Dear @raghav_chadha ,

I know you are doing very well in Parliament by raising small issues that were ignored by most Members of Parliament but have a bigger impact.

I am writing this post regarding an account lien and bank freeze by the Cyber Police of India.

In my case, the issue started when I received a message from my bank branch stating that my account had received a police notice of lien of 6000 rupees. I immediately went to my bank branch and asked them why my account had a lien of 6000 rupees. They followed some procedure and gave me a printout which contained the acknowledgement of my lien. One of the bank employees told me that I should contact the cyber police mentioned on the paper and provide them with the details of the 6000 rupees, such as where it came from and for what reason. However, they did not give me any specific reason why my bank account had received the lien.

Later, I checked my bank statement to find the details of the 6000 rupees transaction and noticed that my case was reported on 6 December 2025, and I had received a transaction of 6000 rupees on the same date. I remember that my neighbour had sent me this 6000 rupees and asked me to withdraw it from the ATM because he had an urgent situation as his mother was going to her village due to an emergency. As a friend, I withdrew the money and gave it to him.

Now I have all the proofs and details to explain to the police, so I emailed all the details to the Bangalore Cyber Cell or the police station where my notice was issued, as mentioned in the acknowledgement given by my bank. However, I did not receive any response. I then tried to contact the investigation officer mentioned in the report. I called several times, keeping a gap of five to six hours out of respect for his time and duties, as they may have many other responsibilities. I also sent him a message on WhatsApp, but there was still no response.

After four to five days, I called again, and this time he picked up the call. He was speaking in the local language, which I did not understand, as I am from Maharashtra and not familiar with the local language of Bangalore. I then started speaking in English, and he told me that I have to come to Bangalore and verify my documents. I explained that for 6000 rupees, it would not be beneficial for me to travel to Bangalore because transportation, food, and stay would cost more than 6000 rupees. He said that he does not know and that I have to come, otherwise he will not issue the No Objection Certificate, and then he ended the call.

This issue may look small, but similar issues are happening everywhere, and no one is noticing them. It feels like “Kare koi aur bhare koi.” Many innocent people face this issue, and it remains unresolved. Because of chain transactions that come into accounts, some people are unable to use their own money. If I travel, I will have to spend more than 6000 rupees to remove the lien. I believe this issue can be resolved through email or online verification, but the investigation officer denied it.

I am also tagging Pushpendra Sir @pushpendrakum and Bangalore Cyber Police @BlrCityPolice . If you could please look into this matter.

Thank you.

Bhai aur beheno, agar aap bhi Binance P2P trading karte ho aur suddenly bank account freeze ho gaya hai toh pareshan mat ho. Yeh bahut common problem hai India mein. Innocent log bhi fas jaate hain jab kisi buyer/seller ka paisa kisi fraud case se link hota hai.

   - Binance P2P complete order history (screenshots)  
   - Buyer/Seller ke saath chat  
   - Payment proof (UPI, bank transfer screenshot)  
   - Bank statement jisme transaction dikhe

 In March 2026, ahead of the Kerala Assembly elections (polling on 9 April 2026), a 2019 Election Commission of India (ECI) letter redistributed by the Kerala Chief Electoral Officer’s (CEO) office was found to carry the seal of the BJP’s Kerala unit. This sparked a political row, followed by police-directed efforts to remove related social media posts

This takedown action itself became controversial, with critics framing it as an attempt to suppress discussion of an official lapse during an election period, while authorities maintained it was necessary to stop the circulation of a withdrawn and erroneous document that was being used to question the ECI’s credibility.The episode remained a flashpoint in the final stretch of the Kerala campaign, with the ECI treating it as a corrected administrative mistake and the opposition presenting it as evidence of deeper concerns about the poll body’s independence.The letter and the seal
The document was an ECI communication dated 19 March 2019 containing guidelines/FAQs on the publicity of candidates’ criminal antecedents (following a Supreme Court judgment). CPI(M) and Congress shared versions online showing the BJP Kerala unit’s seal. It had been circulated by the Kerala CEO’s office to political parties, District Election Officers, and Returning Officers as part of clarifications around mid-March 2026.thesouthfirst.comKerala CEO / ECI explanation:
It was described as a “purely clerical error.” The BJP Kerala unit had approached the CEO’s office seeking clarification on the (by then revised) 2019 guidelines and submitted a photocopy of the original directive that already bore the party’s seal. Staff overlooked this and redistributed that version. The error was identified; on 21 March a formal withdrawal notice was issued telling recipients to disregard the document. An Assistant Section Officer was suspended pending inquiry. Later, a Deputy CEO and a Section Officer were relieved of election-related duties.livemint.comOpposition parties (CPI(M) and Congress) rejected the clerical-error account. They alleged compromised institutional neutrality, claiming seals were being “casually swapped” and questioning whether the ECI and BJP shared the same “power centre.” Some BJP responses labelled the circulation of the old document as misinformation or a political plot.thewire.inDeletion of posts controversyActing on an ECI directive (under the Model Code of Conduct), the Kerala Police cyber cell issued notices to X (Twitter), Facebook, Instagram, and numerous individual accounts. They demanded removal of posts sharing the letter that carried the BJP seal.  Police argued the content insulted the Election Commission, undermined its integrity and transparency, spread false claims about a rectified clerical error, and risked public order or communal harmony by potentially fuelling political division. Reports indicated hundreds of accounts were flagged (approximately 270 on X, 200 on Facebook, and 90 on Instagram). text:
There is a crucial difference between an internet shutdown and a phone jammer. An internet shutdown requires a written order under the Telecommunications Act. A jammer is a radio transmitter that can cut voice calls, SMS and mobile data for everyone within its range. So who gives the Delhi Police the power to switch one on? (1/10)
Read More: https://t.co/kU0KOf2fOY

On 8 September, IFF filed three RTIs with the Delhi Police. We are seeking records on every jammer it possesses, the permissions and procurement documents, the officers authorised to deploy them, the applicable SOPs and deployment registers, and the specific records concerning Jantar Mantar on 20 and 22 July. We have also asked for the records behind the Satya Niketan denial. (9/10)

The question is not whether telecommunications can ever be restricted. Indian law already provides a framework for temporary suspension of services. The question is whether a separate, less visible mechanism can bypass those safeguards and cut communications without the written order, publication, review and accountability that accompany a lawful shutdown. IFF will publish the Delhi Police's replies, including any silence, and continue seeking clarity on who can jam communications, for what purpose and under what law. (10/10)

Ray-Ban Meta glasses struck again. A woman walking home alone was secretly recorded by a man who approached her, then posted the footage on Instagram alongside similar clips of him doing this to other women, as part of "pickup" content.

She's filed a police complaint for stalking and voyeurism. IFF is assisting her with a legal notice to the creator, Instagram, and Meta, the second such notice against Meta in India.

This isn't a one off. It's a design problem.
Read more about it: https://t.co/x5Gzp2NFF0

A woman was followed, stopped on a dark street, secretly recorded through Ray-Ban Meta glasses and turned into an Instagram “pickup” reel that reached over 23 lakh views. Now, our legal notice seeks accountability from both him and Meta. (1/10)

Read More: https://t.co/x5Gzp2NFF0

The legal notice therefore puts Meta on notice not merely as the platform hosting the video, but as the designer, developer, manufacturer, marketer and seller of the glasses. It alleges negligence and product liability, arguing that Meta knew about the pattern of misuse but continued selling the device without an effective way for non-users or people being recorded to report that misuse. (9/10)

The notice seeks removal of every copy, preservation and disclosure of evidence, suspension of monetisation, an account of profits, an apology, and ₹2.05 crore in compensatory and exemplary damages. This case raises a larger question: when a company makes a camera that can be worn like ordinary glasses, who protects the person being recorded? Privacy cannot depend on whether the person being filmed has an Instagram account. (10/10)

The Supreme Court has closed India's Got Latent cases, but the question of an “Influencer Code” is not entirely over. On 14 August 2026, the Court quashed all FIRs arising from the episode and left the “larger issues” of regulating online speech for “another appropriate case”. Here is what that means. (1/7)

Read More: https://t.co/hecp2rl9W4

That qualifier matters. Executive action restricting speech must have a legal basis consistent with Article 19. The Court has previously held that executive instructions cannot independently impose restrictions on fundamental rights. The signed order also contains no finding that the content in question was obscene, nor does it establish a new standard for online speech. (6/7)

For now, there are no guidelines and no pending judicial direction requiring them. But MIB can still attempt regulatory changes, including through amendments to the IT Rules. If it does, IFF will insist on the public consultation promised to the Supreme Court, compliance with the Pre-Legislative Consultation Policy and meaningful participation by affected creators and users. (7/7)

NIXI has changed its justification for suspending chalosansad dot in yet again. The timing matters. The domain was suspended on 22 July. NIXI’s new legal opinion was obtained on 29 August, more than a month later and only after we challenged its earlier reasons. The Supreme Court has repeatedly held that administrative action must stand or fall on the reasons given when the decision was made; authorities cannot ordinarily supplement an order with new reasons after it is challenged. (6/7)

NIXI has now also said that six other .in domains containing “Sansad”, along with other domains containing “Sansad”, “Parliament” or cognate expressions, will be examined. On 8 September, we asked NIXI for a 48-hour standstill on de-registration, deletion, transfer or reallocation of chalosansad dot in, confirmation of Aadhaar deletion, and disclosure of the correspondence it says raised concerns about publication. If no standstill is given, the registrant will approach the court. (7/7)

quotedTweet.text:
On September 10th, 2013, the Supreme Court struck down Section 66A of the IT Act, a vague law that was being used to arrest people for simply expressing dissent online.

11 years later, Maharashtra wants to bring it back in a new form, by amending the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for "online criminal defamation." But defamation is already covered under Section 356 of the BNS, and civil remedies already exist.

So why does the police need this new power? Recent FIRs against citizens and influencers for calling out potholes and infrastructure failures may hold the answer. We've fought this battle before. We don't need a new 66A with a new number.

The Sahyog route also raises a serious constitutional concern. In Shreya Singhal v. Union of India, the Supreme Court upheld Section 69A because the blocking framework contained procedural safeguards, including notice, hearing and a reasoned order. Section 79(3)(b), meanwhile, was read down to require a court order or government notification. A system that blocks first and explains nothing is difficult to reconcile with those safeguards. (9/10)
